Upon the accomplishment of which all perfections arise for human beings;
since there is nothing desired in the three worlds that exists without the body,
therefore, with every effort, let exertion be applied toward it.
The preliminary rite for the administration of elixirs is as follows:
on an auspicious lunar mansion and day, after performing emesis and purgation,
one should then take the liquid from the stalks of the *ketakī* flower for the sake of special purification.
One should drink one *kuḍava* of that [mixture] every three days to remove the defect of *loṇa*;
likewise, one should take *viḍaṅga*, *vacā*, *kuṣṭha*, and *ketakī-stana* combined.
Boiled for three days and drunk, this is the supreme remedy for disorders caused by acidity (amladoṣa).
Śyāmā, agni, viḍaṅga, tryūṣaṇa, triphalā, vṛṣa,
saindhava, devadāru, and mustā— each of these should be taken in equal parts.
One *karṣa* of this linctus with clarified butter, taken for seven days, conquers all defects.
Thus, with the body purified, one should worship the deity, the Guru, the maiden, and the circle of Yoginīs; thereafter, one should perform the alchemical elixir (*rasāyana*).

During the consumption of the elixir, one should follow a wholesome regimen: staying in a windless underground chamber or elsewhere, free from external anxieties, with senses subdued and anger conquered, one should subsist on milk and śāli rice.
One should eat ṣaṣṭikā-rice, barley-food, wheat, mung-bean soup, the meat of wild animals, or pure milk alone;
or one may eat food made with balā, avoiding leafy vegetables and salt.
One should perform an oil massage with whey and likewise bathe in pleasant water.
One should constantly consort with a young woman who is attractive and well-suited to oneself;
for when the lord of mercury (rasendra) is consumed, a man becomes blinded by passion.
For without sexual intercourse, his nutrient essence (rasa) becomes undigested;
from that indigestion arise trembling, burning sensations, pain, hiccups, fainting, fever, restlessness, cough, dyspnea, anorexia, vomiting, vertigo, and delusion. || 13 ||
Therefore, one should cultivate the auspicious and avoid the inauspicious.
Among the things to be avoided in the practice of *rasāyana* are:
anointing with pungent oil, sour gruel (*kāñjika*), wine, and curd.
The meaning is that it removes the defects produced by the consumption of salt.
She whose hair is curled, who is dark-complexioned, and whose eyes are like lotuses— [to her belongs] the circle of deities (devatācakra).
Beautiful, youthful, with broad and well-developed hips, her chest compressed by the weight of her full breasts and bent low; she is tender in the touch of kissing and embracing, and soft-spoken.

That woman who is beautifully adorned with a vulva resembling an *aśvattha* leaf and who menstruates during the dark fortnight is known as a *kākinī*; she is excellent for the application of mercury-binding and for alchemy (*rasāyana*).

One should avoid the bilva, chatrāka, vārtāka, vidala, kākamācikā, radish, garlic, and anything that is pungent, cold, or hot. One should also renounce staying awake at night, sleeping during the day, and sexual intercourse.
One should avoid quarrels, agitation, anxiety, and grief. From the improper administration of elixirs (rasāyana) and medical treatments, pain, sleepiness, lethargy, fever, and restlessness may arise.
For its pacification, one should drink that [juice] with water along with the fruit of the karkaṭī for three days;
or one should lick the powder of śuṇṭhī and saindhava salt with the acidic juices of mātuluṅga;
or, for its pacification, one should drink sauvarcala salt with the urine of cows. (18–19)

One should boil vandhyākarkoṭakī, puṅkhā, and pātālagaruḍī with eight times their weight of water; then one should drink an eighth part of that decoction along with rock salt for three days. This, as spoken by Śiva, destroys all disorders.

One should drink for three days either the root of *kāravallī* or rock salt (*saindhava*) in a dose of one *karṣa*, with the urine of cows; this conquers all disorders. This has been prescribed for those who consume *rasa* and indulge in unwholesome habits.
One should indeed perform this very same procedure in the practice of *rasāyana*;
for nectar (*amṛta*) when conjoined with the proper rite is life-giving, but when devoid of the rite it is poison.
(23) [This is] the transference of mercury (*rasasaṅkrāmaṇa*).
One should eat the four types of nutmeg (*cāturjātaka*), camphor, *kaṅkola*, and *kaṭukī* fruit combined with betel leaf; this is beneficial for the transference of the mercury-essence.
(24) The procedure for the death of mercury.

Now, the correct method for the initial killing of mercury (pārada) will be explained here— whether it be the "facing" (samukha) mercury or that which has been "perfumed" (vāsanāmukhita). Then, one should gradually digest gold in equal proportions, as previously described.
Having added an equal amount of sulfur to that [mercury], one should lick it with the juices of divine herbs,
along with *mātuluṅga* and ginger;
"kha-puṅkhām" means *śarapuṅkhām* (the *śarapuṅkhā* plant).

One should grind the rock salt with a quarter part of that [substance] in a mortar for three days; then, having sealed it in a crucible, one should heat it in a fire of dried cow-dung for a day and night, or for three nights in a fire of chaff.

One should again rub the heated [substance] with an equal amount of seeds produced from divine herbs for four watches (yāmas) in a mortar; then, having sealed it in a *vajramūṣā* crucible, one should heat it by blowing.
That indeed becomes "ash-mercury" (*bhasmasūta*), which is to be employed in all elixirs (*rasāyana*).
The second method for the killing of mercury: one should grind purified mercury with an equal amount of gold and acidic liquids for one *yāma*.
Having washed it, one should cause a paste (*piṣṭī*) to form; then, add half as much purified sulfur to that paste.
Having added half a part of sulphur (gandhārdha) and borax (ṭaṅkaṇa), along with turmeric (haridrīkā) equal in amount to all [the other ingredients],
one should grind everything together with menstrual blood (strīpuṣpa) and the juice of plantain (rambhā).
At the end of the day, having formed it into a ball (golaka), one should cook it in a sand-bath (vālukāyantra).
Having extracted that indeed with a mild fire over the course of a day, one should grind it into powder;
having added an equal portion of powdered sulfur, one should cook it in a *garbhayantra* for three days.
By means of a chaff fire, due to its lightness, the mercury is reduced to ashes.
The third method for the killing of mercury: pure mercury shall be three parts and copper powder one part;
one should grind them with acidic liquids for one day, wash it, and then obtain the paste (piṣṭi).
One should prepare the washed essence of honey (mākṣika) so that it becomes equal to a paste;
all of this should be rubbed for three days with the juice of *cakramarda* leaves.
That ball, placed inside a crucible (*garbhayantra*), should then be heated for three days over a fire of chaff.

Or one may cook it day and night in a fire of dried cow dung until it reaches the state of ash; this is the fourth method for killing mercury. Equal parts of purified mercury, the essence of mica, and gold [should be taken]. (36)
Having added an equal amount of viḍa salt, it should be rubbed with the juice of plantain for one day;
then it should be rubbed for two days with an equal amount of the seeds of divine herbs.
Placed within a *garbhayantra*, it should be cooked in a *puṭa* as before, and it dies [is killed].
The mercury ash (sūtabhasma) [is placed] in a *gaḍukā* apparatus along with divine medicinal juices.
One part of pure mercury and three parts of sulfur should be cooked over fire;
this is the characteristic of the *garbhayantra* (inner vessel apparatus).
It should be four finger-breadths long and three finger-breadths in width.
Having fashioned a clay casket, one should cause it to be dried in the shade. There should be twenty parts of salt and one part of guggulu resin.
Then, having ground everything with liquids and smeared the interior of a casket (sampuṭa) with that same paste, one should confine the mercury therein; this becomes the "womb-yantra" (garbhayantra).
This is the fifth method for the killing of mercury.
One should grind pure, stainless mercury with an equal amount of the juice of *nirguṇḍī* for three days, and then place it inside a glass flask (*kācakūpī*).
In the absence of a glass flask, one should instead confine it within a sealed crucible (*śrāvasampuṭa*).

One should cook it in a sand-vessel (vālukāyantra) for four watches (yāmas), and it will become dead [mercury]. This is the sixth method for the killing of mercury. One part of purified sulphur is equal to the essence washed from *mākṣika* ore.
Equal parts of the two [substances] and pure mercury should be rubbed with the juice of *nirguṇḍī* for one day.
This entire mass, formed into a ball and sealed within a *vajramūṣā* crucible, should be cooked in a *vālukāyantra* for one day; it will then become dead (calcined) and red in color.
The seventh method for the killing of mercury:
equal amounts of purified sulfur should be applied above and below the pure mercury; then, the juice of *kākamācī* is added again inside a sealed crucible (*pakvamūṣā*). (45)
Having added four times the amount of the two [substances] and covered it, one should cook it slowly over a gradual fire in a sand-vessel (vālukāyantra) for four watches; it will then become dead.
This is the eighth method for the killing of mercury.

One should grind purified mercury for one day with the milky sap of either snuhī or hemavallī, along with an equal amount of sulphur; then, having placed it inside a *garbhayantra*, one should heat it in a *puṭa*.
Following the previously mentioned sequence, once it is dead, one should employ it in medicinal formulations.
The ninth method for the killing of mercury: equal parts of pure mercury, *guñjā*, lac, wool, honey, and *ṭaṅkaṇa*—
all of this should be ground together with the juices of *bhṛṅgarāja* for one day.
When placed in a *vajramūṣā* crucible and blown with a bellows, it dies, becoming as white as the moon.
This is the tenth method for the killing of mercury;
[it may also be done] with the juices of *kīṭamāriṇī* or with the juices of *ajamodā*.
One should grind purified mercury with equal parts of sulphur for three days using either the juices of *ahimārī* or the juices of white *aṅkola*; then,
having sealed it in an earthen crucible, one should heat it in a fire of dried cow-dung cakes day and night.
Or else, one should cook it with the fire of chaff; then, after three days, it certainly dies.
This is the eleventh method for the killing of mercury:
take equal parts of purified, dead mercury and diamond in a heated mortar. (52)
One should rub [the substance] with the juices of *haṃsapādī* for three days and then extract it;
one should then coat a *vajramūṣā* crucible with the seeds of divine medicinal herbs. Having sealed the previously mentioned liquid within it, one should heat it for three days with a fire of chaff.

Having cooked and extracted [the mercury], one should take an equal amount of pure mercury (śuddhapārada). Having combined these and ground them firmly for three days with the juices of *haṃsapādī*, one should cook that globule as before; it becomes beautifully liquefied (mṛta). || 54–55 ||
The procedure for the killing of diamond and other substances is explained by way of extension:

the killing of the eight metals, such as diamond and mica, should be understood in the section on mercury (rasakhaṇḍa) or in the section on the primary metals (vādikhaṇḍa), just as it has been stated in the context of alchemy (rasāyana). || 56 ||
The qualities of the essence of death are as follows:
thus, the excellent mercury, when dead, becomes the supreme nectar;
those who constantly serve it will indeed possess this firmly.
It suddenly creates for the celestial beauties a body that is eternally most beautiful and fit for play.
Thus ends the first instruction, titled "The Killing of Mercury," in the section on alchemy (*rasāyana*) within the *Rasaratnākara* composed by the Siddha Nityanātha, son of Śrī Pārvatī.

By kings who know the Dharma, who are devoted to Śiva, who delight in their own duty, and who are great practitioners,
this body must be constantly protected by means of the divine elixir until the limit of the end of the aeon; for from this accumulation of infinite merit, liberation shall arise.
I shall now describe that most wonderful [teaching], which bestows happiness and imperial sovereignty upon the wise.
For the purpose of transforming the body into a sacred field (kṣetra),
one should first consume mica (abhraka) that has been killed and turned into nectar.
For one month, indeed, it should be rendered "field-less" for the purpose of making it a field.
Since mercury is a field of essence (rasa), one should therefore prepare an elixir (rasāyana);
for if it is not made into a field, mercury, though nectar, turns into poison.
How can there be the attainment of fruit for him, just as with a good seed in barren soil?
One should prepare equal parts of the ash of *vajra* and *pārada*, which is like mercury within a diamond cage. 4.

All dead mercury and gold should be ground for a period of days with the juices of *haṃsapādī*; having sealed that mass in a crucible, one should roast it. Then, after grinding it again with the milks of *arka*, one should cook it likewise in a "gaja-puṭa" (elephant-seal) furnace.
One should consume it starting with a quantity increased by a mustard seed, increasing it until it reaches the size of a māṣa.
This elixir, Vajrapañjara, is a refuge for practitioners;
it consists of citraka, fresh ginger, rock salt, mercury, iron, and suvarcala.
All [substances] should always be consumed in equal proportions; this is beneficial for the process of transference (*krāmaṇa*).
By practicing this for six months, one shall live as long as the moon and stars endure, free from wrinkles and grey hair, possessing a divine body and great strength.
In the Vajreśvararasa,
one should prepare dead diamond (vajra) in a twelve-fold proportion relative to dead mercury (mṛtasūta);
dead iron (kānta) equal to the sum of those two, and dead mica (abhraka) equal to the iron.
All of that should be rubbed and infused for three days with the juices of *bhṛṅgarāja*.
Then, for three days, it should be infused with the juices of *gokṣura* and honey; thereafter, one should lick a *māṣa* dose.
This elixir, named Vajreśvara, makes the bodies of men as hard as adamant.
The body of the illustrious ones possesses the splendor of infinite merit and enjoyment;
indeed, by four months [of practice], it destroys old age and one shall live for the duration of a day of Brahmā.
One should powder the five parts (roots, bark, leaves, flowers, and fruits) of *bhṛṅgarāja* equal in measure to *triphalā*.
One *pala* of this should be licked with honey; it is a supreme promoter of vitality (*krāmaka*), like the essence of the thunderbolt’s edge.
The ash of vajra, sūta, abhra, and gold, along with purified mākṣika,
should be ground firmly for seven days with the juices of divine herbs.
Having sealed it, one should cook it again for three days in a vālukāyantra.
Having extracted [the juice], it should be processed for three days with the liquids of *bhṛṅga* and *sarpākṣī*.
One should lick one *māṣa* of this "thunderbolt-edged" essence (*vajradhārārasa*) with honey and ghee.
By using it for six months, a man becomes equal to Rudra.
Free from wrinkles and grey hair, possessing the speed of the wind and great strength—
[one becomes so]. Punarnavā, bhṛṅga, sesame, and vājigandhā, taken in equal parts and combined with an amount of sugar equal to the total, should be powdered and consumed in a pala [of weight].
Bhairavarasa,
gold, mercury, and iron filings— all these should be equal in quantity and processed for three days with the juice of the roots of śatāvarī.
Having impregnated it for three days with decoctions of triphalā and for three days with the juice of bhṛṅga,
one should consume the Bhairava-rasa with honey and ghee.
Taking it one māṣa at a time for the duration of a year, one shall live as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
One should drink one *pala* each of the powdered root of *śatāvarī* combined with the milk of a black goat; this is an excellent, beneficial,
and progressive tonic known as *śilāvīrarasa*.
One should grind together an equal amount of mercury-ash, sulphur, bitumen, and amlavetasa for one *yāma*;
then, mixing it with honey and ghee, one should lick it—one *niṣka* at a time—for the duration of a year. This is the great elixir known as *śilāvīra*.
One who drinks half a *pala* of *muśalī* powder with the juice of *bhṛṅgarāja*, or with the juice of *dhātrī* fruits, quickly destroys old age and shall live for three hundred years;
furthermore, *heman* should be used as a digestive stimulant (*krāmaka*) and an after-drink (*anupāna*).
One should grind pure mercury with the juices of *meghanāda* for three days using the essence of the ocean of nectar (*amṛtārṇava-rasa*).
Then, one should prepare a powder consisting of equal parts of *viḍaṅga*, the two types of *niśā*, and *vyoṣa*.
The root of *āragvadha* should be twice the amount of the powder.
Ghee should be twice the amount of the powder, and honey four times that amount.
Having added everything to the previously prepared juice, one should cook it over a gentle fire while stirring.
One who drinks the ocean of nectar should consume that bolus, one karṣa at a time;
within a year it destroys old age, and he shall live for three hundred years.
One should drink one karṣa of bākucī powder with the juice of dhātrī fruits.
One should grind mercury from Udayāditya with twice its amount of purified sulphur, along with all [the other ingredients],
in a mortar using the juices of *muṇḍī* and fresh ginger for twenty-one days, repeatedly.
One should place this equal amount of pure copper inside a crucible,
seal it, wrap it with a piece of cloth, and coat the exterior with *vajramṛttikā* clay; having dried it thoroughly, one should cook it in a *gajapuṭa*.
Having extracted [the juice] and crushed it into a powder, one should macerate it for three days with the juices of *devadālī*,
and for three days each with the juices of *bhaṅgī* and *punarnavā*.
Then, having added an equal amount of powdered *nāgara* (ginger) along with honey and clarified butter, [it should be consumed].
One should regularly consume two *lihas* of this for a period of one year;
this supreme elixir, like the rising sun, removes old age and death.
One should take equal parts of the powder of *punarnavā*, *devadālī*, and *bhṛṅga*.
One should lick one karṣa of this with honey and clarified butter; it is the supreme *krāmaṇa* (transmuting agent).
Gaganēśvara-rasa consists of mercury, mica, iron, and steel, all processed (*mārita*) in equal proportions. (34)
One should macerate [the powder] for three days in the shade with the juices of *bhṛṅga* and *dhātrī* fruits;
then, having combined everything in equal parts with sugar, honey, and clarified butter, one should seal it in a vessel.
After it has remained in a heap of grain for a month, [one should take] three *niṣkas* of that equal mixture.
One should eat [the powder] and drink one karṣa of milk following the triphalā; at night, one should consume ginger and pippalī. In one year, one becomes immortal;
the hero lives for a day of Brahmā, and this elixir is Gaganēśvara.
One should grind equal parts of sulphur and purified mercury with the milky sap of the banyan tree for three days;
then one should cook it in an earthen vessel over a fire of banyan wood for five hours. (38)
Repeatedly stirring the *vaṭa*-milk with that very wood,
one should remove it and soak it for three days in the juice of *devadālī* leaves.
During the hot season, one should take a single *guñjā* dose combined with a betel leaf.
One should always consume it in increasing doses with the waxing moon, up to sixteen *guñjās*.
One should lick one *karṣa* of the powder of *uttaravāruṇī*, *bākucī*, and *devadālī* with honey and clarified butter; this is indeed an aphrodisiac when used as a post-digestive drink.
By taking it for just one year, it destroys old age; one shall live for three hundred years.
This elixir named Vaṭeśvara makes the bodies of men as firm as adamant.
(42) [This is] Acaleśvararasa.
One should always lick one *karṣa* of dead mercury, purified sulfur, *triphalā*, and *guggulu* in equal parts, mixed with *vātāri-taila*.
Within six months, it destroys old age, and one shall live for three days of Brahmā.
By means of its urine and dung, copper becomes gold.
(44) Having cooked the testicles of a goat in cow's milk during the night, one should drink them mixed with sugar; this elixir is the Lord of Mountains. (45)
Equal parts of the essence of *parameśvara*, mercury, *vajra*, killed *muṇḍa* (iron) with a golden luster,
purified *mākṣika*, and purified sulfur should all be combined with the juices of *jambīra* fruits. || 46 ||
One should grind it in a mortar for seven days, then place that ball in a sealed crucible and roast it in a *bhūdharayantra* for one day; this is known as the supreme *siddharasa*.
One *māṣa* should be licked with honey; after a year, it removes death and old age.
A man becomes a perfected being with a divine body, possessing the prowess of Viṣṇu.
One should always drink white *pauṣkara* root ground with milk, or eat it together with sugar; it is a supreme elixir for sexual vigor.
In the supreme lord Kha,
one should mix purified sulfur, which is twice the amount of the dead mercury, with the essence of the nectar of fragrance.
Having ground it for one day with the juices of kanyākanda, one should seal it.
One should cook one niṣka of it with honey for one day and lick it with honey;
this elixir named Gandhāmṛta-rasa shall conquer death within a year.
One should powder the *bhṛṅgarāja* plant along with its roots after it has been dried in the shade;
the powder of *triphalā* should be equal to that, and sugar should be equal to the total amount. Having mixed these together, one should consume one *pala* at a time as a vehicle for the medicine.
The juice of *kālakaṇṭaka*,
mercury, and iron pyrite (abhraka) in equal parts, with an amount of sulfur equal to the sum of those two—
grind all of this for seven days with the juices of *mṛgaśṛṅgī*.
Having processed it six times with *aṅkuli* oils, one should then consume a dose of one *māṣa*. This elixir, known as *kālakaṇṭaka*, should be taken for one year;
after grinding the leaves of the *karañja* tree, one should drink them with cow's milk as an after-drink.

A man who is completely liberated from old age and death shall live for a day of Brahmā by means of the elixir of the Lord of Immortality (Amṛteśarasa), which consists of dead mercury, mica, magnetite, poison, cinnabar, and bitumen. 56.
One should always lick three *guñjā* seeds mixed with equal parts of honey and ghee;
within six months, this man destroys old age and may live for a *brahmā-dina*.
One should take the powder of *aśvagandhā* root, equal in measure to seven parts of ghee.
One should add eight parts of jaggery and one part of long pepper (pippalī) to it;
having formed it into a mass, one should consume a pala of it over a mild fire for the sake of attaining the success of Amṛteśa Rasarāja, which is indeed a promoter of vitality.
One should add three times the amount of purified sulfur to the purified mercury (sūta),
and then one should throw in an equal amount of mercury to the powder of iron *parpaṭikā*. (60)
All of that should be ground with the milky sap of *snuhī* and *arka* for three days; once dried and placed in a sealed vessel, it should be cooked over a fire of dried cow dung day and night.
(61) [With the oil of *bākucī*—variant reading.]
Then, having added ṭaṅkaṇa and glass (kāca) and sealed it, one should heat it strongly; one who is a hero among alchemists should consume one *guñjā* of this great elixir with honey.
Within a single year, it destroys old age, and he shall live as long as the moon and stars endure.
One should drink one karṣa of the powder of Muśalī root with the juice of Guñjā leaves, or indeed with goat’s urine; this is the supreme *krāmaka* known as Kāñcāyana-rasa. || 63 ||
One should grind the fragrance (gandha) equal in weight to dead mercury with the juices of *kākamācī* for one day;
having sealed it in a crucible, one should cook it in a fire of dried cow dung day and night.
Then, having ground it for one day with the juices of the leaves of divine herbs (*divyauṣadha*), one should seal it again.

Therefore, having extracted the mercury from that [base metal] and combined it with an equal amount of dead gold (hāṭaka), one should lick a single māṣa of this mixture with ghee for the duration of a year;
this true *kāñcāyana* elixir quickly destroys old age and death.

The powder derived from *dhātrī* (myrobalan) fruits should be infused with the juices of *kākamācī*. One should consume one *karṣa* of it with honey; it is a supreme aphrodisiac, the essence of supreme bliss.
Equal parts of dead mercury,
mica, and sulfur should be ground for seven days with the juice of *śigru* roots; this mass should be placed inside a vessel, sealed, and cooked over a mild fire using *śāka* wood for one day.
One should always lick *parānanda*, which is called *rasa*, with clarified butter;
for one day, one should thoroughly cook *kuṣṭha* with decoctions of *triphalā*.
Once it is dried and powdered, one should subsequently lick one *karṣa* of it with honey and clarified butter.
By practicing this for one year, one may live as long as the moon and stars endure.
Mahākālarasa consists of equal parts of processed mercury and mica, with an equal amount of processed iron added to those two.
One should purify the portion of iron and process the sulphur for seven days;
all of that should then be processed separately with the decoctions of triphalā, and with the juices of bhṛṅga, śigru, kacchu, and citraka, seven times each in succession.
One should powder it after having processed it seven times with decoctions of *kaṭukī*; then one should consume equal parts of powdered *karavīra* and powdered *kaṇā* along with aged jaggery.
One should eat all [the ingredients] combined, one *niṣka* at a time, for the duration of a year;
this is the great time-elixir (*mahākāla-rasa*) which strikes fear into old age and death.
Following this, one should consume *tilaka*, *uraṇṭa*, and leaves with jaggery.
The mercury of the gold-foil (hemaparpaṭaka) should be equal in weight to the iron-foil (lohaparpaṭaka) that has been killed by mercury; then,
three times the amount of mercury, along with sulphur, should all be processed with the juices of divine medicinal herbs.
Having sealed that [crucible] for a day, the mercury, once ground, should be heated and thus become bound.
Having added a quarter-part of dead gold to it,
one should grind it for one watch (yāma) with the juices of fire-citron and ginger, and then pulverize it with the three pungents (vyoṣa), cumin, and rock salt.
One should consume an equal amount of the previous elixir along with one *niṣka* of gold each day; this "gold-leaf" elixir (*hemaparpaṭaka-rasa*) quickly destroys old age and death.
One should soak *yaṣṭimadhu* equal in weight to *aśvagandhā* in the juice of *dhātrī* fruits for a day.
One should have one *pala* of this processed [substance] licked with honey; it is a supreme promoter of digestion (*krāmaka*).
Śrīkaṇṭharasa consists of equal parts of gold, silver, copper, sunstone (*sūryakānta*), or iron, all of which have been killed [by calcination].

Take equal parts of the essence of black clouds (kṛṣṇābhrasattva) and antimony (mākṣika), each being equal in weight to the gold. All of this should be sealed and smelted; then, one should add an equal amount of killed mercury and a quarter-part of killed diamond to that resulting mass.
One should grind everything with the juices of *jambīra* in a heated mortar for one day; then, having sealed it, one should cook it in a *bhūdhara* (earth-oven) for a day.
Having extracted it, one should add an equal amount of sulfur, seal it again, and heat it quickly.
One should always lick that powder, in a dose of one *māṣa*, with honey and clarified butter.
This elixir named Śrīkaṇṭha bestows the power of moving through the sky (*khecaratva*);
by practicing it for a year, one may live until the end of a kalpa.
By means of his urine and feces, one should cause all metals and one *pala* of sulfur to be transmuted with milk, followed by the administration of the *krāmaka*.
This is the *khecarabaddha-rasa*.
One part of pure copper, twelve parts of pure mercury,
and three parts of the essence of *bhūnāga*— one should combine these together.
All of this should be ground for one day in a heated mortar (*taptakhalva*) with the juices of *jambīra* fruits.
Having placed all of that into a tortoise-shaped apparatus (kacchapa-yantre),

one should add an equal amount of sulphur ground with the juice of *kāsamarda*, seal it, and cook it in a closed crucible (*puṭa*) until it is consumed; in this manner, the sulphur becomes six times its original weight.
One should digest it by means of gradual application, then extract it and grind it for one watch (yāma) with the juices of *jambīra* fruits; thereafter, the mercury,
from which all impurities have been removed (*niścandra*), should be given to the juice together with an equal amount of *amlavetasa*.
Having added a sixteenth part of *taptakhala*, *caṇakāmla*, *tālaka*,
and *kāsīsa* in the ratio of one-tenth, it should be ground for the duration of a day; then,
having placed all of that in a sealed crucible (*pakvamūṣā*), one should bind it with a cloth.
One should cook it for three days over a mild fire in a *dolāyantra* using *sāranāla*;
having removed it, one should wash it with warm *kāñjika*. If it is not digested [by the stomach], one should cook it in a *kacchapa* type of apparatus along with *viḍa* salt.
In this manner, the sky-like [mercury] should be processed again and again until it becomes equal to the essence (sūta).
Then, having smeared gold leaves with peacock bile and added them in a proportion of one-sixty-fourth part, one should grind them in a mortar.
One should cause it to sweat in the apparatus as before, and once it has been digested, one should add gold;
in this manner, gold to the extent of a sixteenth part should indeed be made to digest within the mercury.
Then, dead diamond to the extent of a sixteenth part should be digested, just like the gold.

Then, after grinding that [mercury] with *tālaka*, *kāsīsa*, and *jambīra*, one should subsequently grind that mercury for three days with the juices of divine herbs (*divyauṣadhi*). It should be heated while enclosed within a *vajramūṣā* crucible; once bound, it should be powdered again. (97–98)
One should consume a dose the size of a *guñjā* seed along with honey and sugar;
this elixir, when bound as a *khecarī*, shall conquer death within six months.
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one will possess great strength and prowess.
One should macerate nīlī, muṇḍī, and the three myrobalans for seven days in juices extracted from beeswax; thereafter, one should lick a karṣa measure of this with honey and ghee.
This is *svayamarinarasa*.
One should reduce pure mercury and sulfur into two parts into a mortar, making them as black as collyrium.
To these, one should add an equal amount of iron powder (kānta), or sharp steel (tīkṣṇa), or even common iron (muṇḍa);
having combined everything, one should grind it in a mortar with the juice of kanyā.
Having formed a ball for one day, one should place it in a copper vessel and cover it with castor leaves; in half a watch (yāma), it will become intensely hot.
One should then place it in a heap of grain and retrieve it at the end of two days.
Kanyā, bhṛṅgī, kākamācī, muṇḍī, nirguṇḍī,
citraka, koraṇṭa, bākucī, brāhmī, sahadevī, punarnavā, śālmalī, vijayā, and dhūrta— using the juices of these [plants] individually, one should [proceed]. (104–105)

It should be processed seven times with each of the seven decoctions derived from the three fruits (triphalā); then, having been processed, the powder of nutmeg (jātīphala) and clove (lavaṅga) should be ground.
One should likewise grind the nine ingredients—trikaṭu, triphalā, and elā—in equal parts.
One should daily lick one *karṣa* of that powder and the previous powder mixed with honey for one year to pacify old age and death;
this is the "Self-Arising Mercury" (*svayamagnirasa*), which has come down through the tradition of the perfected ones (*siddhas*).
One should lick half a *pala* of the powder of sesame and *aśvagandhā* with honey.
*Kakṣapuṭa*, *rasa*, *nirguṇḍī*, *nīlikā*, *vajrī*, *brahmadaṇḍī*, and *tridaṇḍikā* [are the ingredients]. (109)
Śatapuṣpā, mudgaparṇī, śvetārka, vānarī, jayā, peṭārī, kṛṣṇadhattūra, vijayā, and kṣīrakandaka—
[the substance] should be rubbed with all these ingredients together or individually for three days.
Pure mercury should be processed as a paste in a heated mortar with *kṣīrakanda*,
or alternatively with *vajrakanda*; having sealed it with its marrow and then with clay, one should seal that bulb in a *vajramūṣā* crucible and cook it in a mild *puṭa*.

The mercury should be rubbed and cooked again in this manner seven times in succession; this is known as *kakṣapuṭa*. One should lick a single *guñjā* of it with honey, and one shall live for the duration of a day of Brahmā, free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Within one year, without a doubt, a man shall become a body of mercury (rasakāya).

One should take one pala of the powder of *bhallātaka* seeds along with *hayagandhā*, *amṛtā*, and clarified butter as a post-digestive tonic (*anupāna*); this is supremely beneficial for promoting digestion.

Take equal parts of each of the following: mahāśakti-rasa, processed mercury (mṛtasūta), mica (abhraka), diamond (vajra), magnetite (kānta), silver (tāra), copper (arka), gold (hāṭaka), and iron (tīkṣṇa); then add an amount of sulfur (gandhaka) equal to the total weight of all these ingredients. 116.
One should rub everything with *pālāśa* oil for seven days; this is called the Mahāśakti-rasa. One should always eat one māṣa of it with honey.
Within six months, it destroys old age, and one shall live for three Brahma-days.
For seven kalpas he lives for a full year; of this there is no doubt.
Possessing the power of his own will, he becomes a great Siddha equal to the Supreme Śakti.
By means of his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
Oil produced from *pālāśa* seeds, eight *palas* in weight, should be licked with honey;
this is indeed a digestive stimulant (*krāmaka*) that serves as a post-digestive drink (*anupāna*), as clearly revealed according to one's capacity.
(120) This is the *Nāṭakeśvara-rasa*.
One *pala* of killed *vaikrānta*— either red or black—
and one *pala* of gold powder, along with two *palas* of pure mercury,
all of this should be ground for one day with the urine of a young widow.
Śarapuṅkhā, meṣaśṛṅgī, sarpākṣī,
kaṭutumbikā, and indravāruṇikā— one should grind [the mercury] with the juices of these for three days.
Having enclosed that ball in a *garbhayantra*, one should cook it for three days.
Having extracted it with its lightness by means of a fire of chaff, one should grind it;
then, having impregnated it seven times with juices of *bhṛṅga*, one should grind it again.
One should mix the powder equally with the three myrobalans (*triphalā*), the three pungents (*tryūṣaṇa*), honey, and clarified butter.
One should always eat a single *māṣa* [of this]; this elixir is Nāṭakeśvara.
It completely destroys all diseases, old age, and death within a year;
possessing divine luster and a great body, one shall live as long as the moon and stars.
One should drink two *niṣkas* of the root-bark of the *brahmavṛkṣa*, dried in the shade and powdered, with buttermilk; this is a supreme and auspicious aphrodisiac (*krāmaka*).
[With] *triphalā*, *uṣaṇa*, honey, and ghee... [kha].
Hāṭakeśvara:
Bālasundararasa consists of pure white vaikrānta, which should be infused in the sun for seven days.
Ground with *amlavetasa*, it attains a liquid state by that very means.
This liquid, equal parts of purified mercury and honey, should be rubbed for three days and licked in the measure of one *māṣa*; after a month, the man becomes like a child.
Within a year, one becomes equal to Brahmā; this "Bālasundara" elixir should be followed by licking one karṣa of *vākucī* seeds with honey and clarified butter.
(130) This is the Brahmapañjara-rasa.
One should grind four *palas* of pure mercury and one *pala* of dead gold (*mṛtahāṭaka*) for three days in a heated mortar (*taptakhalva*) with the juices of *palāśa* buds and their oils,
along with an equal amount of sulfur.
One should place the purified substance into that [vessel] and grind it for a day with the previously mentioned ingredients.
One should eat a pill the size of a *māṣa* seed; from this, one becomes a conqueror of death within a year.
This hero’s elixir, the "Brahma-cage," enables one to live for the duration of a Brahma-day.
One should take equal parts of the powdered seeds arising from *vānarī* and *kākātuṇḍī*,
and macerate them for three days with the juices of the bark and leaves of *śālmalī*.
Then, having macerated [the mixture] for another three days with the juices of *bhṛṅga*, one should powder it.
One should consume one karṣa of this, equal to ancient jaggery.
Having caused the bhūnāgas to be extracted from red earth, one should test the Śivāmṛtarasa.
If blood comes out during the excision, one should diligently take hold of those [limbs].
One should cook them with an equal amount of black-colored cow-ghee in a metal vessel, stirring them until they take on the color of vermilion. || 136–137 ||

All of that is reduced to ashes; dead mercury is equal to that. Stirring it all with honey, one should increase the dose by half a *guñjā* at a time, and thereafter always consume one *guñjā* until the end of a year.

The elixir named Śivāmṛtarasa removes old age and death for men; it bestows a lifespan equal to a day of Brahmā. One should subsequently cause [the patient] to drink Śivāmbu along with sesame seeds. 139. [With] sesame seeds... kha.
Thus, having worshipped those whose perfected bodies I have seen— bodies made through the power of manifold practices by means of auspicious, essential, and most excellent divine elixirs—
and having extracted the entire essence from them as well as from the scriptures;
This has indeed been declared for the benefit of kings, the learned, and those of great intelligence.

Thus ends the second instruction, titled "The Attainment of the Body by Means of Divine Mercury," in the fourth section on Alchemy (*rasāyana*) of the *Rasaratnākara* composed by the Siddha Nityanātha, son of Pārvatī.
Now begins the third instruction.

The divine medicinal pill and elixir (*rasāyana*) do not succeed if devoid of the transmuting agent (*krāmaṇa*); therefore, let it be used as a vehicle for the sake of transmutation, for it indeed brings about swift success.
1. The Pill that Restores the Dead to Life (*mṛtasañjīvanī-guṭikā*).
Having ground equal parts each of *kākatumbī*, *kākamācī*, *nirguṇḍī*, *kumārikā*, *gojihvā*, rock salt (*saindhava*), *guñjā*, and fresh ginger (*ārdraka*),
one should smear the crucible with that paste to a depth of one finger-breadth.
Mercury, the essence of *vyoma*, *kānta* iron, *tīkṣṇa* iron, *muṇḍa* iron, and the essence of *tāpya*—
all these in equal parts— one should grind them together and macerate them for one day with the juices of *jambīra* fruits, then place the mixture into a crucible (*mūṣā*).
Having coated [the vessel] and plastered it with a paste, one should seal it and dry it;
then, having cooked it in a *karīṣa* fire for a day and night within a *puṭa*, one should remove it.
Again, having placed it in a plastered crucible and sealed it, one should then cook it in a *puṭa*.
Having thus smeared the ten crucibles, one should cook [the mixture].
A divine pill, the supreme reviver of the dead, is produced.
When held in the mouth, on the head, at the throat, in the ear, or in the hand, [it grants immortality].
Properly wrapped in gold, it is supreme for arresting the aging process;
it destroys wrinkles, graying hair, the fire of time, and the fear of death.
Without a doubt, after only one year, one shall live for three hundred years.
One should always drink one pala of pure fragrance with cow's milk;
by means of this after-drink (anupāna), the essence enters the body and indeed brings about the perfection of the body.
This Vajreśvarī-guṭikā removes all affliction; it consists of mercury, iron, muṇḍaloha, and the essence of mica, combined with an equal portion of gold. || 10 ||
One should grind equal parts of heated sattva, dead vajra, and all [other ingredients] with juices of *jambīra* for seven days; having formed a ball (*gola*), one should extract it.
[Then add] *nirguṇḍī*, rock salt, honey, *gojihvā*, and *kākatuṇḍikā*.
Having ground it, one should smear the ball on all sides to the thickness of one finger.
Having sealed it in a vajra-mūṣā crucible, one should cook it for one yāma in a bhūdhara furnace.
After smearing and sealing it again, it should be cooked in this manner for as long as a fortnight.
One should smear the crucible with well-ground *yavaciñcā*, *palāśa*, *rājī*, and cotton seeds; then, having placed the aforementioned ball inside it,
one should add *ṭaṅkaṇa* and white glass and seal the top.
One should heat it with the application of acacia charcoal until it becomes liquefied.
Then, one should place it in a crucible smeared with *biḍa* salt and add an equal amount of gold; one should repeatedly blow upon it while it is being heated until the gold is digested.

When the gold has been digested, one should extract it and grind it in a heated mortar for three days with the juices of divine herbs; having sealed it in a *vajramūṣā* crucible, one should heat it by blowing.
There arises a supreme, divine pill known by the name Vajreśvarī.
Remaining in the mouth, it indeed destroys old age and death within a year;
it causes the paralysis of weapons and bestows the lifespan of Brahmā with certainty.
Having taken Sahadevī on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, one should grind it into a fine powder.
One should eat one *karṣa* with clarified butter; it is beneficial when taken in gradual succession.
This is the *vajrasundarī* pill: [it consists of] red *meghanāda*, as well as *pāṣāṇabheda*. (20)
Having ground [the ingredients] together with breast milk, one should smear the crucible with it;
then, having placed one part of dead-vajra and sixteen parts of gold powder into it, one should close it and blow it firmly for the duration of one watch (yāma).
Having taken it out, one should place pure mercury equal in quantity into a mortar;
one should seal the cavity with the pastes and grind it with the juice of ginger until it forms a ball (golaka).
Taking the bulb of the Caṇḍālī plant, one should grind it well with breast milk.
Having smeared the *golaka* with this, one should seal it within a diamond crucible (*vajramūṣā*).
After heating it in a "gaja" (elephant) fire-pit (*gajapuṭa*), the pill known as Vajrasundarī should be extracted.
If one holds [the powder] in the mouth for one year, one shall live for three days of Brahmā;
one should daily drink one *pala* of the bark-powder of the *brahmavṛkṣa* with milk.
Indeed, this digestive stimulant (*krāmaṇa*) as a post-drink bestows great success upon the practitioner.
Indeed, copper smeared with the impurities arising from that, through smelting, becomes divine gold; this is the truth spoken by Śaṅkara. [This is] the Hemasundarīvaṭikā pill.

One should digest an equal amount of gold with the face-to-face mercury (samukha-rasendra) using the *viḍa* formulation as before. Then, having ground it for three days with divine herbs and cow's urine, one should blow it in a sealed crucible (*vajramūṣā*).
Having extracted it, one should hold the *guṭikā* named *Hemasundarī* in the mouth;
thereafter, one should lick half a *pala* of sulphur with twice as much clarified butter.
Within one year, it destroys old age, and one shall live as long as the moon and stars endure.
The Vajrakhecarī pill consists of pure mercury, dead iron, *vyomasattva*, and *sahāṭaka* (gold);
one should grind all these in equal parts with the group of acidic substances for three days.
Having made that ball firm, one should then dry it in the shade. Then,
having ground together equal parts of *brahmakārpāsa* seeds, black mustard, *yavaciñcikā*, and *vandhyā*, one should smear the previous ball with this paste.

Having sealed it in a *gajapuṭa* and cooked it, one should then extract it and apply it as a paste; having sealed it again in a crucible (*mūṣā*), one should heat it intensely. Thus arises the *vajrakhecarī* pill. When held in the mouth, it destroys death within a year.

One *pala* of powdered *bhūtāravaṭa* mixed with sugar should be consumed for the purpose of transference (*krāmaṇa*); the man’s lifespan becomes equal to that of Brahmā. Having thrown it [into a mortar], one should grind it again with the juices of fresh ginger.
Surasundarī is Kha-bhūtāvaraṭacūṇa; Vyomasundarī is Vaṭikā.
Pure mercury should be rubbed for one day with the leaf-juices of *kārpāsī*, *kākamācī*, and *kanyā*, then washed with acidic liquids and extracted;
four *niṣkas* of that juice and half a *niṣka* of copper powder [should be combined]. || 35–36 ||
One should grind together three-quarters of a niṣka of mercury, one-quarter of gold, and an equal amount of powdered iron filings with acidic juices;
at the end of the day, having formed a ball, one should place it inside a jambīra fruit.
One should cook it for three days in a *dolaka* apparatus using *sāranālaka*.
Having extracted it, one should hold the pill, called *vyomasundarī*, in the mouth;
after only a year, it destroys old age, and the man shall live for the duration of a day of Brahmā.
Having stirred the powder of *citramūla* with honey in a vessel of *kāntaloha*, one should consume one *karṣa*; this is beneficial for the purpose of transference (*krāmaṇa*).
This is the *Hāṭakeśvarī-guṭikā*.
One *niṣka* of gold leaf, three *niṣkas* of pure mercury,
and the juices extracted from *jambīra* and *śarapuṅkhā* should be mixed together for a full day. That resulting mass should be bound in cloth and cooked in cow’s milk.
In the swinging apparatus (dolāyantra), the pill known as Hāṭakeśvarī is produced day and night. When worn in the mouth, it destroys old age and death;
after just one year, without a doubt, a man shall live for ten thousand years.
One should lick one *pala* of *triphalā* powder, processed for a single day with decoctions of *khadira* seeds and mixed with honey and ghee;
this is the *arkaprabhāvatī* pill, which promotes sexual vigor. (44)

Three pure niṣkas of mercury and one niṣka of copper powder should be ground in a mortar for a day with the sour juice of tamarind and buttermilk. That mass should then be bound in cloth and placed within a vessel filled with buttermilk and tamarind juice.
One should cook it in a dolāyantra for one day; the resulting pill possesses the brilliance of the sun.
If held in the mouth for one year, a man becomes equal to the sun.
[One should take] one karṣa of oil extracted from the seeds of the Palāśa tree with cow's milk.
Indeed, this "Surasundarī" pill is an excellent digestive aid and a supreme remover of old age and death;
it contains one part gold, one part iron, five parts silver, and two parts mercury. (48)
One part in three of *vyomasattva* (mica essence) and one part in six of copper powder—
having made all of this fine, one should grind it for three days in a heated mortar (*taptakhalva*) with the group of acidic substances (*amlavarga*) and *kāñjika* in a *dolāyantra*.
One should cook that bolus for three days; it becomes the pill known as Surasundarī.
When worn in the mouth, after a year it removes death and old age.
Thereafter, one should drink one karṣa of the root of the Bhūtāravaṭa tree with milk.
Vajratuṇḍāvaṭikā, gold, silver, copper, iron, tin, lead, and the essence of mica— all these in equal parts, along with a portion of powdered mercury and dead-vajra (sublimated mercury). || 52 ||
One should grind equal parts of pure mercury and all the juices of divine herbs for one day, then seal it in a *vajramūṣā* crucible and heat it;
this pill, known as *Vajratuṇḍī*, is produced when held in the mouth.
It is said that within a year it destroys old age, death, and the multitude of weapons;
one becomes a great hero with a body like adamant and shall live for three hundred years.
One should extract the juice of a young girl and stir it together with molasses.
One *pala* of this is to be licked as a digestive stimulant and always used as a post-digestive drink; it is indeed the *Kāmasundarī* pill.
One part of gold powder and three parts of purified mercury [are to be combined]. (56)

One part of dead *vajra* (diamond) should be ground for the duration of a day in a heated mortar (*taptakhalva*) with the juices extracted from milk-tubers (*kṣīrakanda*) and those arising from *devadālī*,
along with an equal amount of *kānta* iron powder; indeed, one should grind them together.
The substance to be smelted, enclosed within a diamond crucible, becomes the pill known as Kāmasundarī.
When worn in the mouth for a year, it removes death and old age.
[One should take] three niṣkas of Brahma-oil and two palas of cow’s milk.
One should drink this mixture as an after-potion; the man will then attain a lifespan of one hundred thousand years.
[This is] the Bhūtāvaraṭa root and the Gandhārī pill.
When the mercury has melted in an iron vessel, one should add mercury equal to one-fourth the weight of the mercury;
stirring it slightly with a wooden stick, one should remove it from the heat after a muhūrta.
[Then add] śatāvarī, kṣīrakanda, vajravallī, and indravāruṇī.
Pāṭhā, punarnavā, ciñcā, lāṅgalī, and suradālikā—
having strained these with a cloth, one should grind [the mercury] with their juices for three days. In that vessel, using an iron pestle, it should be dried in the shade and made into pills.
Having enclosed it within an iron casket and firmly sealed the joint with clay and salt,
one should blow it in khadira charcoal until it becomes bright red and then remove it; having repeatedly dug out from the middle of that [mass], one should extract that essence once again.
One should cook [the ingredients] combined with glass (kāca) and borax (ṭaṅkaṇa), sealed within a crucible (mūṣā).
This perfected Gāndhārī pill, when always kept in the mouth for a year, [bestows longevity].
One should administer one karṣa of the oil from the seeds of Kākatuṇḍī as a nasal drop (nasya).
Indeed, this digestive stimulant as an after-drink shall enable one to live for a thousand years.
The Mārtaṇḍī pill is prepared by rubbing equal parts of purified mercury and sulfur until they form a collyrium-like paste (kajjalī).
Having enclosed it within a copper casket and sealed it firmly with salt and clay,

one should dry it and cook it for one watch (three hours) over a lamp-fire in a crucible of ash. Then, having extracted that [substance] which has adhered to the upper part of the casket, one should grind it.

Combined with an equal amount of mercury, one should cook it in a sealed crucible (sampuṭa) as before. Having extracted it and combined it with an equal amount of mercury, one should grind it and cook it again; in this manner, one should repeat the process with mercury and borax seven times.
One should add equal amounts [of the ingredients] to it and rub the whole for a day;
having placed it in a *vajramūṣā* crucible and sealed it, when heated, the mercury becomes a solid bolus (*khoṭa*).
This is indeed the *Mārtaṇḍī* pill; for whomsoever it remains in the mouth for one year, [it grants immortality].
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, he shall live as long as the moon and stars.
One *pala* of oil produced from *palāśa* seeds, mixed with an equal amount of milk, should be drunk daily as a transmuting agent (*krāmaṇa*); by that very moment, one becomes unconscious.
One should powder that [substance] when dry with a blazing fire; it is bound by the void (kha).
One should pour cow’s milk drop by drop into its mouth;
once it has awakened, milk and food should be given, which is most beneficial for its nourishment.
By means of its urine and excrement, copper becomes gold.
The great adept Vāyuvega beholds the earth as having openings.
The pill of Tārakeśvarī consists of mercury and talaka in equal parts, with the juices of kākamācī and amṛtā.
One should rub it for one day, form a pill, and dry it thoroughly.
One should place it in a vajra-mūṣā crucible, cover it with iron parpaṭas, seal the joint, and heat it intensely; thus the mercury becomes fixed as a solid bolus (khoṭa).
Having administered the iron-foil (lohaparpaṭaka), it should likewise be swallowed three times;
for one year, this pill, the Mistress of the Stars (tārakeśvarī), should be held in the mouth.
Afterwards, one should drink one karṣa of Bākucī seeds with cow's milk.
One should purify Vidyāvāgīśvarī-guṭikā,
the essence of space (vyomasattva), dead diamond (mṛtavajra), gold, silver, copper, and human bone; then,
having purified sharp iron, magnetite, and orpiment, one should mix them together.

One should take equal parts of all these fine powders and an amount of pure mercury equal to the portion of the powder; having rubbed them together with the group of sour substances (amlavarga) for three days, one should seal the mixture in a crucible and heat it.
This pill, known as Vidyāvāgīśvarī, remains effective for the duration of a year.
For one in whose mouth it resides, old age and death do not exist;
one should always drink one *karṣa* of *jyotiṣmatī* oil for the purpose of transference (*krāmaṇa*).
Such a wise person becomes a master of speech and may live as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.
Vajratuṇḍāvaṭikā,
kāntapāṣāṇa, mākṣika, ṭaṅkaṇa, and karkaṭāsthi,
along with the milks of snuhī and arka and bhūnāga— all of these should be taken in equal parts.
One should rub [the ingredients] with breast milk for a day and smear that mixture onto the crucible.
Having placed an equal amount of molten mercury and an equal amount of diamond ash (vajrabhasma) inside it, one should seal it and cook it in a "Gaja" type furnace for just one watch (yāma).
Then, having placed pure mercury (kha) into a smeared crucible and sealed it, one should heat it vigorously with the juices of parpaṭī. Pure mercury (kha).
In this manner, the process should be repeated again and again until the *vajrasūta* (adamantine mercury) is thoroughly fused.
Then, an equal amount of glass (*kāca*) together with *ṭaṅkaṇa* (borax) should be added to that very [substance].
In this way, adding equal portions each time, one should blow the furnace repeatedly for a hundred crucible-fusions (*mūṣā*).
This mass of splendor, this lord of mercury (rasendra), becomes like the sun;
this pill, Vajratuṇḍā by name, destroys death when held in the mouth.
Within just one year, without a doubt, a man shall become equal to Rudra.
From its urine and feces, gold is produced as before.
One should consume five parts of a karṣa [weight] with honey and ghee; this is the Gaganeshvari pill of Rudanti.
Having ground together borax, crab shells, wool, realgar, lac,

and the wax from the ears and eyes of a buffalo, along with breast milk of a woman, one should place the essence of mica (abhrasattva) into a crucible smeared with that mixture and blow it [with a bellows]. || 90–91 ||

One should cast into that [crucible] an amount equal to the *sattva*, as before, along with molten *sāra* and the juice of divine medicinal herbs; having placed it right there, one should blow upon it.
It becomes united and bound, as previously described, by means of glass (*kāca*) and borax (*ṭaṅkaṇa*).
When blown in a hundred crucibles, this mass of brilliance becomes the mercury.
If one holds it in the mouth for one year, that person becomes equal to Śiva.
This pill, Gaganeshvari, brings about freedom from old age and death.
One should drink one niṣka of oil extracted from bilva seeds;
thereby, digestive fire arises in the stomach. One should drink milk again and again.
[This results in] the direct recollection of past lives, poetic genius, and the retention of what has been heard.
The state of moving through the sky and invisibility arise; there is no doubt in this matter.
[The ingredients are] the bliss-pill (ānandaguṭikā), agnimantha, vajravallī, sūraṇa, and vanasūraṇa.

One should grind purified mercury with the juices of these [plants] and Citraka for the duration of a day in a heated mortar (taptakhalva). Then, one should take one pala of that mercury and add one pala each of Tāla and Vaṅga, along with all of those together with Amlavetasa.
Having made that ball again, one should rub it for one day with pure mercury as before;
then, having prepared a lead crucible weighing four palas, one should place it therein. || 99 ||
One should seal it within a crucible made of four *pala* of pure copper;

having enclosed it in an earthen crucible, one should then perform a *puṭa* with wild lotuses (*āraṇyotpalaka*) measuring two hundred [in weight]. When it has cooled to the temperature of its own body, one should extract it.
One should grind everything with the juices of divine medicinal herbs for three days. Then, one should prepare pills weighing four *niṣkas* each, dry them,
and having sealed each one individually in a *vajramūṣā* crucible, heat it with a fierce fire.

Indeed, this pill of bliss, when held in the mouth, destroys death; there is no doubt that for one year one shall live for three days of Brahmā. Oil extracted from the seeds of *vātāri* (Artemisia) [should be taken] in a measure of one niṣka with cow’s milk.
One should drink this daily for the purpose of translocation (*krāmaṇa*); it is supreme and brings about swift accomplishment.
(This is) the Vajrakhecarī pill:
mercury equal in weight to diamond-ash is processed with the juices of *haṃsapādī* for three days.
Having rubbed the *dvandva* mixture in a smeared crucible and sealed it (*andhita*), one should subject it to the *bhūdhara* type of *puṭa* for a day and night. Then, having extracted it,
one should indeed add a portion of mercury equal to the previous amount and process it for three days with the juices of *haṃsapādī*.

Having ground it in a crucible smeared with *dvandva* (binary compound) and sealed (*andhita*), one should blow it; that residue (*khoṭa*) should be purified by blowing, through the application of glass and *ṭaṅkaṇa*.
It should be blown again and again until it attains the luster of a star.
Having thoroughly processed that mercury, the essence of space (vyomasattva), and gold in equal parts,
one should then prepare a pill to be placed within the mouth;
known as Vajrakhecarī, it destroys death after one year.
A man shall become free from wrinkles and grey hair and possess a divine body;
he should drink one *karṣa* of the powder of *nirguṇḍī* and *muni* with clarified butter.
This is the *Ratneśvarī* pill.
One should grind equal parts of *kānta* iron and copper together, place them in a *vajramūṣā* crucible, and blow them with a bellows until they form a solid mass (*khoṭa*).

This perfected powder should then be rubbed with sulfur and sour gruel (*amlavetasa*), properly sealed in a crucible, and cooked by means of a *puṭa*; having removed it from the fire, one should then rub it once more.
Following the sequence as before, one should seal fourteen crucibles.
One should color the gold, which has been paired with a diamond, using this very [substance];
while blowing [the fire], one should thus add equal amounts seven times into the middle of the crucible.
That powder of the *khoṭa* should be processed with women’s menses for a number of days; then, one should grind all that equal amount of quicksilver for one watch (*yāma*).
One should wrap it in birch bark, bind it in cloth, and cook it for three days.
One should extract the globule produced in the *dolāyantra* from the concentrated liquid (*sāranāla*).
Then, one should envelop that previous globule with a paste made from the combined mass of *gāndhārī*, *jīvanī*, *lāṅgalī*, and *indravāruṇī*.
Having blinded it for a day, one should cook it in the earthen vessel (bhūdhara) and then extract it;
it should be smeared again and cooked again for a period of fourteen days. Thus, a divine pill arises, known by the name Ratneśvarī.
If it remains in the mouth for only one year, a man becomes equal to Nandin.
Possessing divine luster and great strength, he shall live for thousands of years.
This applies to one in whose mouth it remains for as long as twelve years.
Through contact with his perspiration, the eight metals become gold; there is no doubt in this, for it is the truth spoken by the Lord.
Afterwards, one should lick the powder of the five limbs mixed with honey and clarified butter, along with the substance arising from *rudantī*.
Divya-khecarī-vaṭikā:

Take equal parts of gold, the essence of black mica, silver, and copper, and grind them into a fine powder. Having smeared a crucible with the double-paste (dvandvabandha), place the powder inside, seal it, and heat it in a furnace.
That cinnabar (tatkhoṭa) [weighing] four parts and one part of "dead-vajra" (mṛtavajraka),

along with one part each of *mākṣika*, *tīkṣṇa*, and *kānta*— all finely powdered— should be placed in a crucible smeared with a mixture of two [substances], closed, and blown [with a blowpipe]. || 122–123 ||
That powder, having been finely ground, should be mixed with one part of molten mercury and rubbed for three days in a heated mortar (taptakhalva) with the juices of divine herbs. Then,
having sealed it, one should cook it in a bhūdhara [digester] and extract it after twenty-four hours.
Having added an equal amount of molten mercury again, one should grind it and likewise subject it to *puṭa* firing.
In this manner, having added molten mercury in equal amounts seven times and having ground it, one should cook it in *puṭa*; thus, the mercury is reduced to ash.
Having added sulfur equal in weight to the ash-mercury and having sealed it, one should heat it strongly;
a divine pill arises, renowned as the "Divyakhecarī.
If one holds it in the mouth for one year, one shall live for a thousand kalpas.

By smearing all types of iron with his urine and feces, divine gold is produced; there is no doubt that it remains so even after being melted down. One should always drink two palas of the substance from the *bhṛṅgarāja* plant as a follow-up.
One should always lick the aforementioned ash-mercury in a dose of one *guñjā*,
with honey and clarified butter, for one year; the man will then attain a lifespan of a hundred thousand years,
free from wrinkles and graying hair, and endowed with great strength and prowess.
Mercury bound with gold and vaikrānta should digest gold and the essence of vaikrānta in a state of binary union (dvandvita) within the mercury,
until they become equal in proportion; thereafter, one should cause it to flow through that very [mixture].
It becomes bound by the Equal One; one should always hold it in the mouth. By practicing this for a year, one conquers old age, time, and untimely death.
Following this, one should drink a decoction made from the petals of the Kumārī plant mixed with sugar.
This pill of vaikrānta, bound with gold, bestows the lifespan of Brahmā upon men; one should grind purified mercury with a portion equal to the essence of vaikrānta. (134)
Having smeared that ball with the juices of divine medicinal herbs for a day and secured it with a chain, one should seal it inside a diamond-crucible (vajramūṣā) filled with salt.
One should dry the joint in the shade for three days using a fire of chaff.
Or one should heat it in a fire of dried cow-dung for a day and night, then remove it;
having smeared that ball with a binding agent and likewise enclosed it, one should dry it in the shade and then heat it intensely; it will certainly attain a firm bond.
If one holds this Vaikrānta pill in the mouth for one year, one shall live for three days of Brahmā;
indeed, this pill bestows the fruits of all desires.
Afterward, one should lick one Karṣa of Triphalā powder with honey and clarified butter.
One should cause [the mercury] to digest [the powder]; by means of gold, one should make a vajra combined with the divine khecarī pill, and that should be reduced to a fine powder. (139)
O Guhyasūti, this should be placed one-quarter part above and below in the crucible; having carefully sealed the joint, one should dry it thoroughly.
One should cook it for a day in the [furnace] called Bhūdhara, and then, having extracted it, one should grind it.
Having confined [the substance] in a heated mortar for a day with the juices of divine medicinal fruits,
one should then cook it in an earthen crucible (bhūdhara) for a day and roast it with mild *puṭa* applications.
Having removed it, one should again grind it in that same manner and confine it for three days.

This mercury, having been slowly sweated with chaff-fire while being turned over from top to bottom, becomes "ash-mercury" (bhasmasūta); one should employ it in all formulations. One part of the liquefied mercury and one part of the aforementioned ash [should be taken].
One part of pure nāga should be ground with all [the other ingredients] using acid;
it should be placed in a blind crucible (andhamūṣā) and heated until it becomes a solid mass (khoṭa), which is that mercury.
One should heat it in an open crucible (prakaṭamūṣā) until the nāga is completely consumed.
Having liquefied this mercury by means of the method for melting the ore,
one should place it in a kacchapa apparatus after adding a *biḍa* salt in a tenfold proportion;
then, one should digest all the metals, such as gold and others, in their proper sequence.
Thereafter, one should digest each [ingredient] sixfold, and then digest the pair of vajras.
This should continue until it becomes threefold; then, one should gradually digest the gems, each melted separately, threefold at a time.

Then, having extracted [the substance] from the apparatus and ground it for a day with the juices of divine herbs, one should seal it and heat it intensely; thus an auspicious pill (*guṭikā*) is produced.
One should worship this with the *Aṅkuśī* mantras; by name, she is the Divine Sky-farer (*Divyakhecarī*).
Indeed, he in whose mouth this resides shall become equal to Bhairava;

possessing divine splendor and a massive body, he travels by means of the power of moving through the air (khecaratva), and wherever he desires, right there he sports with women and other companions. || 150–151 ||
It remains for as long as the end of a great kalpa, without a doubt;
by his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
Palāśa flower powder, black sesame seeds, and sugar [are used].
One should eat all three *palas* daily; this is beneficial for the process of transmutation (*krāmaṇa*).
One should add an equal amount of the powder of *pracaṇḍakhecarī-guṭikā* and horse-hoof iron to the secret mercury.

One should grind all of that firmly for three days with the acidic juice of *mātuluṅga*. Then, having added dead *vajra* equal in weight to the mercury (*sūta*), one should grind it in a heated mortar (*taptakhalva*) with acids for a day. That ball should then be sealed and fired in a *puṭa* furnace.
Having placed one part of the previously prepared mercury in a crucible apparatus for one day, one should grind it firmly with the juice of *mātuluṅga* for a day; then,
having sealed it as before, one should cook it, and mercury should be added again.
It should be rubbed and cooked as before, and this should be done seven times. By repeatedly adding the liquid, it becomes "dead mercury" (bhasmasūtaka);
one should employ it in all formulations, for it removes old age and death.
One part of powdered nāga, one part of the previous ash,
and one part of molten mercury— one should form a *khoṭa* as before.
Likewise, when the nāga has been incinerated, one should again digest the molten [mercury] within it.
As before, ending with iron and gems, when worn bound upon the mouth, this pill named Pracaṇḍakhecarī grants the power of movement through the sky;
by means of it, the hero obtains, as before, a fruit that is exceedingly difficult to attain. (160–161)

One should drink one karṣa of the powder of nirguṇḍī root with buttermilk; thereafter, the Kaṅkālakhecarī pill should be administered, along with a sixteenth part (kalāṃśa) of purified mercury and dead vajra. || 162 ||
Having ground all of that with the group of acidic substances (amlavarga) in a heated mortar for three days,
one should then smear the leaves of the mature seed with it in equal proportions, and then again with the petals of the sun-plant (bhānu).
Having sealed them, one should then bury them within the interior of a furnace;
having covered them there, one should burn a wood fire for three days.
Then, having extracted them, one should seal them in a crucible smeared with a pair [of substances].
One should cook it in a *puṭa* over a fire of dried cow-dung for a day and night, then remove it;
once it has been liquefied, one should melt it again and cast this equal amount into mercury that has been opened by the mouth of a crucible (*vāsanāmukha*). (166)

One should grind it with sour juice for one *yāma*; once formed, one should take the resulting ball (*gola*), place it inside a *jambīra* fruit, tie it in a cloth, and cook it for three days in a *dolāyantra* using *sāranāla*.
A beautiful pill (*guṭikā*) is thus produced.
Known by the name Kaṅkālakhecarī, she resides in the mouth and destroys death.
He who retains [this practice] for one year shall live for a day of Brahmā;
thereafter, he should lick one karṣa of equal parts of sulphur and guggulu with clarified butter.

One should strongly heat the pill known as Kālavidhvaṃsikā, having first enclosed together equal parts of the essence of black abhraka, kāntaloha, mākṣika, gold, tīkṣṇaloha, and powdered sauvīra. || 170 ||
That powder of the residue should be made into a fine dust equal in weight to the liquefied mercury;
one should grind all of this with acid for one day in a heated mortar, including half as much sublimed diamond (vajra),
and then, having sealed it, cook it in an earthen furnace (bhūdhara).
Having extracted an equal amount of the previous *sūtaka* from the day and night [of processing], and having added it,

one should grind everything with the juices of divine medicinal herbs for the duration of a day; then, as before, one should cook the liquefied mercury again in an earthen vessel for an equal amount of time.

Having added [the ingredients] and ground them, one should cook them again; thus, seven times over, having added an amount of fragrance equal to this ash, one should strongly heat it until it becomes blind (solidified).
A divine pill is produced, which is supreme and destroys old age.
For whomsoever this [mantra] resides in the mouth, what can Death do to him? By the application of six hundred recitations, one may live for a thousand kalpas;
by the mere sweat of his body, all metals turn into gold.
They are born; there is no doubt in this. One should drink the Śivāmbu that causes transmutation.
The Pañcānana pill consists of gold, silver, copper, and iron-ore (kānta), along with an equal amount of sharp powder (tīkṣṇacūrṇa). 177
One should blow upon that *khoṭa* which has been sealed within a crucible smeared with the *dvandvamelāpa*;
having reduced it to powder, it should be consecrated as before. One should digest it in the presence of mercury (*sūta*) gradually until it is five times the amount.
One should indeed grind it for three days with the juices of divine medicinal herbs.
When heated while placed inside a blind crucible (andhamūṣā), an auspicious pill is produced;
it is to be held in the mouth for the duration of a year under the name Pañcānanā.
Freed from wrinkles and graying hair, one may live as long as the moon, sun, and stars,
by taking the *hastikarṇī* plant with its roots, powdered and combined with honey and clarified butter;
having sealed it in a smooth vessel, one should place it within a heap of grain.
Having extracted it after three weeks, one should consume one *pala* as a follow-up.
As for the pills that pierce [the body] a hundred times and so forth, and the various methods of binding mercury mentioned in the *Ṛddhikhaṇḍa*:
In this regard, I shall describe the procedure for piercing the body with that very [substance], just as it is:
one should prepare a divine pill, the size of a jujube fruit or an egg, using various processed and bound "kings of mercury" (rasarāja) individually. 183–184.

That pill, which bestows fruits corresponding to its own nature, should be worn in the mouth for one year; it is a "hundred-piercer" (śatavedhī) pill that grants men a lifespan equal to the duration of a Yuga. A "thousand-piercer" (sahasravedhī) pill protects one through eight kalpas.
That [mudrā] which pierces a hundred thousand targets bestows strength equal to that of Viṣṇu;
that which pierces a million targets grants the station of Rudra; and that which pierces ten million targets brings about the state of Īśvara for men. (186–187)
The *vedhikā* pill pierces ten crores [of atoms] and bestows the state known as Sadā; the pill that pierces a hundred million (*arbudavedhī*) bestows the state of Śrīkaṇṭha;
and the *śaṅkhavedhikā* pill bestows the perfect state of Bhava.
That which is perfected as the "smoke-piercing" (dhūmravedhī) bestows the station of Śakti;
that which performs the "touch-piercing" (sparśavedha) grants the station of Parā-Śakti;
and that which performs the "sound-piercing" (śabdavedha) belongs to him for the duration of a year.
He who has [the mantra] residing in his mouth is indeed perfected; he shall eternally attain the eternal state.
Moving according to his own will, possessing a vajra-body, he cannot be pierced even by vajra-strikes.
From his urine and feces, all metals and gold [are produced].
They are produced through contact with sweat and even from the touch of the body.
For all the aforementioned yogas, pure sulphur (śuddhagandhaka) should follow; "in the section on *kṛddhi*" means in the section on *vādi*.
Likewise, one should daily consume half a *kha* of it; this is beneficial for the transference of the vital essence (*rasa*).
"O Kālī, O Kālī, O Mahākālī, you who feed upon flesh and blood!"
"O Goddess with red and black faces, grant me the perfection of mercury (rasasiddhi), svāhā! With this perfected mantra, one should worship the wheel of Śaktis,
Kālikā, Bhairava, the Siddhas, the Kumārī, and the prepared mercury.
Then one should employ the divine elixir (*rasāyana*) and attain perfection; one should hold the pill in the mouth and constantly recite the aforementioned mantra.
By the application of the mantra over the mercury, one shall swiftly attain perfection.
The method for accomplishing [the goal] at another time:
"That accomplishment at another time which was taught in the Manthānabhairava—for that purpose, one should practice the five principles (tattvas) and the sixth, the living soul (jīva). (197)
Having had union with a Kākinī during her period of menstruation, one should collect it;
the wise know that seed of blood situated in her womb as "Gagana.
The fresh feces and wind of the son born of a Kākinī are called "Sadyovij."
The fire element is the flower of the Kākinī, and the water element is the blood of her son;
the entire body of the son of the Kākinī is said to be the earth element (pṛthivītattva).
The semen arising from the body of the one who partakes of the essence (rasa) is called the life-force (jīva).
Having prepared one *karṣa* of mercury combined with each of those [substances] to achieve a penetration of ten million times (*koṭivedha*),
one should preserve it in a separate state, well-ground and formed into a ball (*golaka*).
It should be raised to the height of a man and half that in width.
One should prepare a copper vessel as thick as six finger-breadths,
which should be firmly attached to the back of the four-faced chamber.
One should then mix cow's ghee and human oil in equal proportions.
Having filled that vessel with that [liquor], one should then worship the *Siddhacakra*.

One should satisfy the Virgin (*kumārī*), the Guru, the Deity, and the Fire, as well as Bhairava together with Bhairavī, with offerings of meat and blood, and one should worship the Guardian of the Field (*kṣetrapāla*).

possessing divine luster, a massive body, and great strength and prowess.

possessing a body like adamant, he lives—this is the truth, the truth spoken by Śiva.

A celestial chariot (vimāna) half a yojana in width, filled with Apsarases, comes before that perfected one; of this there is no doubt. Seated therein, he sports in the world of Rudra like Bhairava himself.
Free from hunger and thirst, he does not perish even at the destruction of the world;
